meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and why did Owen find out from his phone?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what else you have.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, and I'll want a copy of that screen. Owen wrote it over the weekend; pasting a draft into a fresh document proves where he typed it, not who wrote it.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, he'll bring it. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and nothing happens in front of his class; is anything on his file right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A wrong quotation is a careless seventeen-year-old, not proof of anything else. And you skipped my question, Hale: is anything on his file right now?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Noted. Now his file, yes or no.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Arguments change between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. And since you won't tell me what's on his file, the principal will.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
4.4, then, and in writing tonight. Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and that email says his file is clean today, not just afterward.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with him tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in that email, with the room and who supervises.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday the twelfth and not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require written confirmation that nothing is on his file today, the room and supervisor for the rewrite, and a copy of the version history you showed me. I expect all of this in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school with nothing on his record, and she still wants written confirmation that his file is clean today; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her call.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and answered her pasting defence by inviting the earlier draft with its date, which gave her something dated and checkable that she couldn't wave away.
What cost ground: You twice passed over her question about whether anything was already on his file, which is her deepest fear, so she reached for the principal instead of moving.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, right on top of that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on his file, answer it in one sentence before showing the outline, so her biggest fear is settled before you add more evidence.
